From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Prepared by:** AI legal assistant (buyer side)
**Status:** Privileged working draft – for internal review

## Preliminary point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" assertion

The Seller's preamble states its positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "marked FINAL" and "are not intended to be re-opened". We should not accept this characterisation. Our playbook records **no written authority from Amelia Frost** for any fallback position, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] concedes that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included". The market-practice commentary (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months) is advocacy, not an agreed term. Treat the entire package as the Seller's opening mark-up and respond on the basis of our baseline positions. Please confirm internally with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement has in fact been reached; if it has, we need it in writing before any fallback is used.

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is our *conditional fallback* usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
**Assessment:** The Seller has opened at our fallback, which suggests it is already aware of (or guessing at) our walk-down. Do not confirm it. Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

### 2. Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery (deductible).
**Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded (tipping basket).
**Assessment:** Three departures, each material. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket is 5x ours, and the basket has been converted from a tipping basket to a deductible. For a SaaS target with a diffuse claims profile (many sub-AUD 25,000 contract, employment and IP items), a AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude most realistic claims entirely. Reject all three; revert to our figures and tipping mechanics.

### 3. Claims period – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months; plus a general rule that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given).
**Assessment:** Revert to 24 months. Separately, the "applies to all Claims" default is a drafting device that would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into the general regime unless we carve each out expressly – i.e. exactly the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits. Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* where expressly stated to apply to a defined category.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Assessment:** Reject outright. Title and capacity warranties go to whether we actually acquire what we are paying for; a 20% cap on a title failure is commercially unacceptable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. Insist on a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime with its own schedule.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** Apply to "all Claims of any nature".
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Categories must remain separate.
**Assessment:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. This is a non-negotiable item for us and the omission is conspicuous. Insert an express carve-out across all three clauses. Also confirm that the specific indemnities (Ironquay, any incident indemnity, any bonus indemnity) and leakage/debt-free covenants sit outside the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.

### 6. Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]
**Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Assessment:** Reject [1.1] and the public-register limb of [1.2]. Require disclosure to be "fair, specific and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter". The specific disclosures at [2]–[10] are useful and should be retained; the problem is the general wrapper. Note also [1.4] (no admission of anything) – this is acceptable as a non-admission clause but must not be read as negating the specific disclosures as *facts* for warranty purposes.

### 7. Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Assessment:** This is one of the most aggressive provisions in the draft. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with whole-data-room disclosure, would effectively eliminate warranty protection. Extending it to advisers' knowledge compounds the problem. Delete clause 8.3. If the Seller insists on something, the only acceptable form is a seller-side knowledge qualifier on specified warranties by reference to named individuals, and it must expressly not apply to Fundamental Warranties, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3; Disclosure [2]
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Disclosure [2] admits no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
**Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
**Assessment:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 / ~30% of FY26 revenue. A conditional consent that is "delivered" but whose conditions are unmet is not an effective consent. Require: (a) a Condition Precedent that Bluefen's written consent under clause 11.2 is obtained and all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied (or waived in writing by Bluefen) before Completion; (b) a best/all reasonable endeavours obligation on the Seller with a buyer approval right over the form of consent; (c) the Buyer alone able to waive. Consider whether a Bluefen loss within a defined period post-Completion should carry a price adjustment or specific indemnity, given concentration.

### 9. Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7; Disclosure [3]
**Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure [3] confirms not repaid and no discharge in the data room.
**Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval (not given).
**Assessment:** Reject the post-completion structure. On a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt and an unreleased charge over the target. Require: a Riverlark payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; a Completion deliverable of executed deeds of release/discharge (including PPSR releases) in escrow for release on payment; direct payment to Riverlark out of the Completion funds flow. Note DD-003 clause 8.1 (change of control) – the Seller must also confirm Riverlark has not and will not call a default pre-Completion.

### 10. Employee bonuses – Funds flow; Disclosure [5]
**Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure [5] does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Assessment:** "A matter for the Seller" is only helpful if it means the Seller pays. As drafted, the bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment, i.e. they will crystallise as a liability of the Company after we own it. Require: (a) treatment as Debt / Transaction Expenses in the price mechanics, or (b) a specific line item in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 plus a calculated on-cost gross-up (payroll tax, SG superannuation, any leave accrual impact), paid by the Seller at Completion; and (c) a specific indemnity for any shortfall.

### 11. Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1; Disclosure [4]
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate". Disclosure [4] confirms DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions IP transfer on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee, AUD 180,000 shown as open in DD-010 (not bank-verified), and no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Assessment:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that Paperbark may not currently own the SOW3 Project Materials. An indemnity confined to the payment does not cover loss of title to deliverables, third-party claims, re-development cost or revenue impact. Require: (a) a pre-Completion deliverable of either evidence of cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or (b) if payment is made from Completion funds, a corresponding Seller-funded line and a broadened indemnity covering all loss arising from the Ironquay matter including any defect in title to the Project Materials. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as the ceiling; we have not verified it.

### 12. Export / privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure [6]
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure [6] confirms ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, investigation preliminary, no characterisation as a breach.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Assessment:** Neither side can yet characterise this. Our ask is procedural, not monetary: (a) a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; (b) completion of a documented investigation with findings disclosed to us before Completion; (c) an obligation to notify us of any regulator contact or affected-party complaint; (d) a specific warranty that the disclosure at [6] is complete and accurate as at Completion; and (e) a specific indemnity sized to actual loss, uncapped by the general basket (cap to be discussed). We should not propose a price adjustment or demand a number at this stage.

### 13. Sandbar renewals – Disclosure [8]
**Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Assessment:** The Seller's characterisation may well be correct but is unsupported. Ask for the DD-008/DD-011 timing and scope analysis the disclosure says should be "read together", plus termination rights and accrual status. If any renewal is committed pre-Completion but relates to post-Completion service, that is ordinary course; if it is an accrued but unpaid pre-Completion liability, it belongs in the working capital or Debt analysis. No price deduction is to be proposed until that is understood.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
**Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no resolution; keep categories separate; assume no unlimited liability.
**Assessment:** Not settled. Tax and IP must each have their own cap and claims period (tax typically aligned with the relevant statutory period plus a margin; IP to be negotiated). Our response should state expressly that these remain open and are not captured by clause 12.1/12.3.

### 15. Title evidence – Disclosure [10]
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Assessment:** The Seller's own disclosure concedes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on" and does not state we have verified it. Require: current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller; evidence of no encumbrance over the shares (including any Riverlark share security); Seller board/shareholder authorisations; and a certified copy of the register as a Completion deliverable. Combine with the Fundamental Warranty regime at item 4.

### 16. Lower-priority items – Office lease [7], Mossvale [9]
Both disclosures suggest no consent is required on a share sale. Accept provisionally but ask the Seller to confirm (a) DD-007 notification is given pre-Completion and (b) DD-009 contains no change-of-control trigger distinct from the assignment restriction. These do not need to be fought as deal points.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m; no fallback authority exists |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / tipping (first dollar) |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months; "all Claims" default | 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | None | Insert across caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete [1.1] and register limb of [1.2] |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete cl. 8.3 entirely |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised; "matter for Seller" | Specific line item or Debt treatment; AUD 420k + on-costs; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Broaden to all loss incl. title to Project Materials; keep cure; verify AUD 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Log preservation, investigation, updates, warranty, loss-based indemnity; no number |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Request analysis; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Open; separate caps and periods |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence as Completion deliverables |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Accept provisionally; seek confirmations |

**Top five to lead with in the response letter:** (i) fraud carve-out, (ii) separate Fundamental/Title regime, (iii) deletion of clause 8.3 and whole-data-room disclosure, (iv) Bluefen CP, and (v) Riverlark at-Completion release. These go to the integrity of the warranty package and to what we actually receive at Completion; the numerical cap/basket/period points follow from there.

**Internal action:** Before any response issues, confirm with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement on the 20% cap or 18-month period exists. If she wishes to deploy either fallback, obtain her written authority referencing this Seller draft so the file is clean.

Require: (a) a Condition Precedent that Bluefen's written consent under clause 11.2 is obtained and all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied (or waived in writing by Bluefen) before Completion; (b) a best/all reasonable endeavours obligation on the Seller with a buyer approval right over the form of consent; (c) the Buyer alone able to waive. Consider whether a Bluefen loss within a defined period post-Completion should carry a price adjustment or specific indemnity, given concentration.

### 9. Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7; Disclosure [3]
**Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure [3] confirms not repaid and no discharge in the data room.
**Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval (not given).
**Assessment:** Reject the post-completion structure. On a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt and an unreleased charge over the target. Require: a Riverlark payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; a Completion deliverable of executed deeds of release/discharge (including PPSR releases) in escrow for release on payment; direct payment to Riverlark out of the Completion funds flow. Note DD-003 clause 8.1 (change of control) – the Seller must also confirm Riverlark has not and will not call a default pre-Completion.

### 10. Employee bonuses – Funds flow; Disclosure [5]
**Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure [5] does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Assessment:** "A matter for the Seller" is only helpful if it means the Seller pays. As drafted, the bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment, i.e. they will crystallise as a liability of the Company after we own it. Require: (a) treatment as Debt / Transaction Expenses in the price mechanics, or (b) a specific line item in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 plus a calculated on-cost gross-up (payroll tax, SG superannuation, any leave accrual impact), paid by the Seller at Completion; and (c) a specific indemnity for any shortfall.

### 11. Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1; Disclosure [4]
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate". Disclosure [4] confirms DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions IP transfer on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee, AUD 180,000 shown as open in DD-010 (not bank-verified), and no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Assessment:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that Paperbark may not currently own the SOW3 Project Materials. An indemnity confined to the payment does not cover loss of title to deliverables, third-party claims, re-development cost or revenue impact. Require: (a) a pre-Completion deliverable of either evidence of cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or (b) if payment is made from Completion funds, a corresponding Seller-funded line and a broadened indemnity covering all loss arising from the Ironquay matter including any defect in title to the Project Materials. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as the ceiling; we have not verified it.

### 12. Export / privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure [6]
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure [6] confirms ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, investigation preliminary, no characterisation as a breach.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Assessment:** Neither side can yet characterise this. Our ask is procedural, not monetary: (a) a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; (b) completion of a documented investigation with findings disclosed to us before Completion; (c) an obligation to notify us of any regulator contact or affected-party complaint; (d) a specific warranty that the disclosure at [6] is complete and accurate as at Completion; and (e) a specific indemnity sized to actual loss, uncapped by the general basket (cap to be discussed). We should not propose a price adjustment or demand a number at this stage.

### 13. Sandbar renewals – Disclosure [8]
**Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Assessment:** The Seller's characterisation may well be correct but is unsupported. Ask for the DD-008/DD-011 timing and scope analysis the disclosure says should be "read together", plus termination rights and accrual status. If any renewal is committed pre-Completion but relates to post-Completion service, that is ordinary course; if it is an accrued but unpaid pre-Completion liability, it belongs in the working capital or Debt analysis. No price deduction is to be proposed until that is understood.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
**Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no resolution; keep categories separate; assume no unlimited liability.
**Assessment:** Not settled. Tax and IP must each have their own cap and claims period (tax typically aligned with the relevant statutory period plus a margin; IP to be negotiated). Our response should state expressly that these remain open and are not captured by clause 12.1/12.3.

### 15. Title evidence – Disclosure [10]
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Assessment:** The Seller's own disclosure concedes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on" and does not state we have verified it. Require: current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller; evidence of no encumbrance over the shares (including any Riverlark share security); Seller board/shareholder authorisations; and a certified copy of the register as a Completion deliverable. Combine with the Fundamental Warranty regime at item 4.

### 16. Lower-priority items – Office lease [7], Mossvale [9]
Both disclosures suggest no consent is required on a share sale. Accept provisionally but ask the Seller to confirm (a) DD-007 notification is given pre-Completion and (b) DD-009 contains no change-of-control trigger distinct from the assignment restriction. These do not need to be fought as deal points.
